### Problem addressed

A maintenance method can become obsolete or revise its own acceptance rules merely to declare success.

### Failure mode

A revised oracle or maintenance method provides its own only warrant, silently changing the predecessor obligation or success criterion.

### Mechanism

Revise a method, threshold or oracle only for an authorised failure/benefit hypothesis or separately authorised objective change, using evidence not constituted merely by the candidate satisfying its newly chosen rule; preserve unrelated predecessor obligations.

### Trigger context

The method is failing or disproportionately costly, technology changes, or a candidate proposes to revise the expectation by which it will be judged.

### Non trigger cheap path

Keep an adequate method or remove an unused control; independent warrant need not mean a different person or an infallible external oracle.

### Dependencies preconditions

Evidence of the method’s limits, an authorised revision boundary and a comparison not defined solely by the proposed successor.

### Canonical disposition

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

### Disposition rationale

B-067 already requires an authorised bounded revision and comparison not defined solely by its successor. A-098’s independent oracle warrant is therefore not absent and does not add a separate composition-level invariant after B-029/B-026 are considered. Preserve a specific non-circular warrant for changing expectations, not merely management approval. B’s own evidence calls its compound analytical despite its origin label; correct the canonical provenance without claiming historical authorship.

### Problem addressed

This extrapolates local adverse results to all tools, people and tasks.

### Failure mode

Human-only maintenance is asserted to be intrinsically superior regardless of task, tool quality and total cost.

### Mechanism

Reject the universal comparison; evaluate bounded automation by correct outcomes and complete costs.

### Trigger context

Adjudicate when a negative experiment is used to forbid all maintenance automation.

### Non trigger cheap path

Use whichever simple human/tool combination is supported for the actual task, including no automation.

### Dependencies preconditions

No universal comparison across all maintenance tasks and tools exists in the inspected evidence.

### Problem addressed

Benchmarks and narrow deployments may be treated as proof of durable autonomous understanding, acceptance and operation.

### Failure mode

General unattended maintenance reliability is asserted without adequate cross-task and consequential deployment evidence.

### Mechanism

Withhold the general capability claim; distinguish bounded demonstrated tasks from open obligations in intent, long-term regression, review, authority and deployment.

### Trigger context

A general unattended-maintenance claim is used to remove oversight or transfer responsibility.

### Non trigger cheap path

Use bounded automation with explicit constraints, or an ordinary authorised maintainer when evidence is insufficient.

### Dependencies preconditions

Representative unseen tasks, reliable independent oracles, end-to-end outcomes, long-term follow-up and legitimate operational authority would be needed.

### Problem addressed

Universal boards can add delay and diffuse accountability without improving intent or impact decisions.

### Failure mode

A standing change board is required regardless of the actual coordination and authority problem.

### Mechanism

Strip the mandatory ritual while preserving appropriate authorisation, consultation and evidence; use a fuller forum only when conflicts or obligations require it.

### Trigger context

Adjudicate when the presence of a board is treated as the maintenance property itself.

### Non trigger cheap path

A direct authorised maintainer decision can suffice for a bounded change.

### Dependencies preconditions

A real unresolved cross-party decision or external requirement is needed to justify the fuller form.

### Domain profile

```json

  "CHANGE_INTENT_AND_CHANGE_CLASS": "Adjudicate when the presence of a board is treated as the maintenance property itself. Corrective restores accepted intent; adaptive responds to environment; perfective changes capability or useful qualities; preventive reduces prospective problems. A single intervention can serve several purposes.",
  "BASELINE_AND_AFFECTED_ARTEFACTS": "Identify the system/configuration being changed and any non-code artefact needed to interpret the request. A source commit alone may omit deployed data and obligations.",
  "PRESERVATION_OBLIGATION_AND_OBSERVER": "The decision is adequately authorised and informed whether or not a meeting occurs. Separate the observations that must differ from those that must survive. Current obligation holders, including downstream users where relevant, determine what is accepted rather than copying old tests unquestioningly.",

The maintainer needs enough understanding to interpret the change and recognise disputed assumptions; complete historical reconstruction is not a universal prerequisite.",

### Reconciliation rationale

B explicitly strips a formal board for every change. Legitimate authority and coordination may be required, but a meeting form is neither universal nor equivalent to the underlying property.

### Problem addressed

Prevent cross-mechanism mismatch: correct analysis, tests and implementation of different intended changes.

### Failure mode

Locally valid intent, analysis, evidence and action refer to different interventions or subjects at their handoffs.

### Mechanism

Bind the relevant intent, baseline, candidate, impact boundary, observation/oracle and acceptance/action authority across mechanism handoffs so that evidence is consumed for the same authorised intervention.

### Trigger context

Evidence or decisions pass among stages, tools or actors, or concurrent work can change the subject before action.

### Non trigger cheap path

One visible issue, exact diff and direct check can establish the binding in a local change; no separate contract document or registry is required.

### Canonical disposition

### Disposition rationale

A-093 and the binding facet of B-072 address the same cross-stage join: independently valid intent, baseline, impact, oracle and action can refer to different subjects or obligations. Merge that relational invariant; split B-072 invalidation because matching identity does not prove current applicability.

### Reconciliation rationale

A-093 and the binding facet of B-072 address the same cross-stage join: independently valid intent, baseline, impact, oracle and action can refer to different subjects or obligations. Merge that relational invariant; split B-072 invalidation because matching identity does not prove current applicability.

### Problem addressed

Prevent stale green evidence while avoiding indiscriminate revalidation of everything.

### Failure mode

Correctly identified evidence is consumed after a consequential supporting assumption has become invalid.

### Mechanism

Track the consequential assumptions under which evidence supports a downstream claim; when an assumption changes, narrow or invalidate only dependent claims and obtain adequate replacement evidence before consequential reuse.

### Trigger context

A relevant environment, observer, tool/model, data distribution, dependency or obligation changes while earlier evidence is still being consumed.

### Non trigger cheap path

Reuse evidence when its relevant envelope remains valid; explicit local reasoning may replace a dependency registry or global rerun.

### Disposition rationale

B-072 explicitly covers changed assumptions as well as identity; it is not merely a hash-binding rule. Preserve a distinct invariant: the exact same candidate and oracle can cease to be supported after environment, observer, tool or dependency assumptions change.

### Problem addressed

Transition or integration can create new interactions absent from either endpoint’s separate assessment.

### Failure mode

Locally acceptable edits, versions, mappings or authority transfers form an unacceptable reachable joint state.

### Mechanism

At the join of concurrent edits, mixed versions, data mappings and responsibility transfers, identify reachable combinations that matter to supported obligations and validate, isolate or prohibit those combinations.

### Trigger context

The selected composition creates materially new joint states or interactions not covered by its constituent endpoint evidence.

### Non trigger cheap path

Proven disjointness, a genuine quiescent boundary or a simpler strategy can remove a combination; no exhaustive universal state model is required.

### Dependencies preconditions

A credible account of reachable combinations, sequencing and external actors; abstract state models must match actual operation.

### Domain profile

### Disposition rationale

B-073 survives as cross-domain composition rather than a synonym for A-095 recovery or A-096 completion. Independently accepted concurrent edits, version paths and schema mappings can create new reachable joins with obligations not established by endpoint checks. Inherited one-domain checks are parents, not evidence that every combined state is safe.

### Reconciliation rationale

B-073 survives as cross-domain composition rather than a synonym for A-095 recovery or A-096 completion. Independently accepted concurrent edits, version paths and schema mappings can create new reachable joins with obligations not established by endpoint checks. Inherited one-domain checks are parents, not evidence that every combined state is safe.

### Problem addressed

Prevent the synthesis itself from increasing maintenance burden without commensurate assurance.

### Failure mode

Individually defensible controls combine into duplicated or obsolete burden whose continuing value is not reassessed.

### Mechanism

Evaluate the combined inquiry, validation, coordination and support arrangement against live obligations and observed outcomes; consolidate, substitute or retire controls whose consumer or protection has ended or whose cost is dominated, without silently waiving the outcome.

### Trigger context

Several controls interact, compete for finite maintenance capacity or persist after their original obligations change.

### Non trigger cheap path

Use the existing adequate local method unchanged; a simple cost/consumer judgment can suffice without a meta-process or optimisation engine.

  "Would the cheaper/non-trigger path suffice: Use the existing adequate local method unchanged; a simple cost/consumer judgment can suffice without a meta-process or optimisation engine.",
  "Who actually consumes the result and has legitimate capable authority to act; is non-change, repair, restructuring, migration, restricted servicing or retirement the justified outcome?"
]

### Reconciliation rationale

Equivalent after aligning guards: both judge the combined controls by protected obligation, actual consumer, full cost and feedback, allowing substitution and retirement. A’s “smallest” is not evidence of a global optimum. Retain B’s cautious context-dependent disposition and unvalidated integrated-payoff boundary.
